intro: This page collects research software and computational projects arising from my physics research. For the underlying physics, see [Research](research.html). For broader data science, machine learning and engineering projects, see [Data Science, ML and Engineering](data-engineering.html).

research_projects.title: KEWPIE3
paragraphs: **Objective:** validate and publish KEWPIE3, the new version of the KEWPIE2 code for fusion-evaporation cross-section predictions in superheavy element synthesis.
**Key question:** how can the calculation of the compound nucleus formation probability be improved with Langevin-based stochastic approaches?
research_projects.topics: Scientific computing · Nuclear reaction modelling · High-performance computing · Uncertainty quantification

figures.alt: Eleven panels of predicted evaporation-residue cross sections against centre-of-mass energy for reactions not yet measured, such as titanium-50 and chromium-54 beams on actinide targets. Curves for the 2n to 5n channels are drawn with shaded uncertainty bands, and a red arrow marks the Coulomb barrier energy in each panel.
figures.caption: KEWPIE3 predictions for reactions that have not yet been measured, with uncertainty bands, from the chiSquareLog2 best fit (s0 = 6.65 fm, beta = 1.16 × 10^21^ s^−1^).

figures.alt: Plot of the ratio of calculated to measured evaporation-residue cross sections at the channel maxima, on a logarithmic axis from 0.01 to 100, for targets from neptunium-237 to californium-249. Symbols show the 2n to 5n channels and colours show Dubna, GSI (TASCA) and LBNL data.
figures.caption: Comparison of calculated and measured evaporation-residue cross sections: the ratio of theory to experiment at the channel maxima, by target, channel and laboratory.

research_projects.title: Fusion dynamics
paragraphs: **Objective:** revisit the fusion dynamics in the fusion-by-diffusion model for fusion-evaporation production cross sections.
